independent_assessments.assessment: Every invocation still runs current stored callable metadata, stored binding reservation where applicable, and full bind_lir in their original order before whole-result lookup. Substituted public LIR schema/module/verified fingerprint/target/layouts/functions/resources/closures must therefore fail the same current binding checks. WholeMachine never supplies a VerifiedModule or native preflight authority.

ModuleInput exhaustively projects all TypedModule fields other than functions, including source fingerprint, target, dyn/life inventories, closures/resources and unsupported markers. Function inputs are ordered and complete TypedFunction Eq, including all absolute spans. Exact per-function Entry owners are reused only if their full input equals the current function; spanless native-equality hits with different spans receive a separate exact current snapshot. This prevents old span/header/foreign data from becoming a whole-input proof. Strong retained inputs and COW prevent in-place safe mutation and ABA.

independent_assessments.area: All emitter options, layouts, limits and current roles
independent_assessments.assessment: WholeOptions binds the complete EmitOptions entry, scalar policy, closed collection and requested jobs. Product additionally binds complete Limits, current scalar layouts and exact remaining ledger at the post-binding boundary. Existing fully admitted scalar eligibility is required, with no resources/closures/dyn/life/task domains. Current checked_scalar_domain independently requires empty task interfaces/worker IDs, false task/registration/stored-borrow/owned-sum modes, and no current suspend/export/ownership role for any function. No old VerifiedModule is stored or used to establish these conditions.

Read production emitter/module helper environment accesses: the admitted suffix has no mutable env/filesystem/time input. The test-only alternate copy planner disables whole reuse. Foreign declarations and every header are in the complete function input; no-entry/entry errors and foreign harness conflicts cannot cross option/input equality. Current target and all helper-affecting raw tables/roles are bound or excluded. Generated helpers/runtime/wrappers are shared only inside this narrow closed domain, not inferred from a partial mixed-function cache.

independent_assessments.area: Exact successful result and remaining work
independent_assessments.assessment: Product is recorded only after complete suffix construction and into_items succeeds. It retains one exact raw machine result and collected flag, with spent=post-prefix-before minus successful final remaining. A hit requires the same complete input/options/Limits and exact post-prefix ledger, then subtracts only that recorded spent amount. This is not a renewed allowance. A changed or insufficient before value returns to the original planner, preserving its exact phase/error/remaining amount. Aggregating the successful suffix is valid here because its current inputs and start are identical and it has no other budget-state side effects in the admitted domain.

A real miss discards the historical whole product before rebuilding; prepare also clears it. A failed replacement suffix cannot publish a partial product. Prefix errors may retain an older independently valid raw result, but lookup never runs on that failed current call; later exact recovery can lawfully reuse it. Product and function owners are a single current Session epoch, with no new unbounded history and no saved checker authority. A later native/link failure does not make a valid raw emitter subproduct a native success receipt.

Whole result sharing returns raw machine Module plus current verification fingerprint and remaining ledger. Existing transform/partition/native/object/link/output code still consumes current independently bound inputs and performs its original checks. No native Builder, LLVM verification, object integrity, external linker discovery, cancellation or guarded publication is skipped by this slice.

Whole hits set reused_machine_module and actual input-function comparisons; per-function hits/misses remain zero because those consumers were not invoked. Backend and root JSON expose these separately. Existing warm tests now assert the whole tier rather than incorrectly counting every shared function as a function hit. No whole-request zero-work or allocator count is inferred.
